idiom_name: Result/Option combinators (or_else, unwrap_or_else) plus a modelled degraded state
implementation_notes: Rust makes the fallback a value: Result<T, E> and Option<T> carry the failure, and combinators choose the substitute - unwrap_or_else and map_or_else are lazy, or_else can fall back to a cache, and ? moves the decision to the layer that owns the degradation policy. tokio::time::timeout bounds the attempt, and when the dependency is a service the honest model is an enum (Full | Degraded | Shed) instead of a global flag, so consumers must handle the quality they received. The classic mode object is replaced by that type plus a metrics call at the fallback site.
pitfalls: unwrap_or_else is lazy, but or_else changes the error type: mixing dependency errors needs an error enum or Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync> first.
catch_unwind only catches unwinding panics (never in panic = "abort" builds) and requires UnwindSafe; it is not a substitute for handling the dependency's errors.
Blocking work in an async fallback occupies a runtime worker thread; use spawn_blocking or an async cache.
